records.real_world_identity_notes: Aussie Racing Car: a silhouette racer of the Australian one-make championship, carrying a Chevrolet Camaro body on a purpose-built steel tubular spaceframe and powered by a second-hand Yamaha FJR1300 motorcycle engine of about 1.3 litres. The gearbox is integral to that motorcycle unit and is operated by a sequential quick-shift lever mounted close to the steering wheel. The Camaro body is a silhouette, so Chevrolet is not the manufacturer of this car.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.
records.identity_basis: The championship's own FAQ establishes the car and its sequential gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
records.specification_basis: The championship states a sequential gearbox on a quick-shift lever, and the drive selected five gears through a sequential stick. The count was then confirmed in-game by the driver, and it agrees with the donor motorcycle: the FJR1300 is a five-speed until 2016 and these engines are bought second-hand.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established five gears through a sequential stick, the standing-start clutch, the clutchless running shift, automatic cut, and no automatic blip. The gear count was separately confirmed in-game because a guided drive establishes only the highest gear actually selected.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.
A community AMS2 database lists six gears. The drive found five, the driver confirmed five in-game, and the donor FJR1300 is a five-speed before 2016, so five is recorded.

The downshift blip is required because a motorcycle-derived racing sequential engages by dogs rather than synchronisers. Descriptions of the championship car as having a dog engagement gearbox appear in search results attributed to the championship, but could not be retrieved from its site, so that wording is not cited as a source and the construction remains an inference. A source showing a synchronised gearbox would make the blip optional.

The championship describes gears being changed as quickly as the driver can lift and re-depress the throttle, while the drive found an automatic cut in AMS2. The simulator behaviour is recorded as observed; the description may reflect driver practice rather than a required lift.
